result.title: SWAM: State-aware World Action Model for Multi-Agent 3D Environments
result.summary: Interactive world models generate virtual environments autoregressively from player actions and visual history. However, visual history alone cannot reliably capture the evolving states of independently acting non-player characters (NPCs) in real games, particularly when they are outside the camera view. Recent multi-agent world models address this challenge through joint multi-view generation or persistent shared state, but often rely on external observations, like maps or scene geometry, or predefined state transitions. We present SWAM, a State-aware World Action Model that separates agent-state evolution from autoregressive visual generation in interactive 3D environments. A lightweight state model propagates character dynamics from actions without consuming generated frames, combining motion priors with learned scene-dependent corrections. The predicted states then guide an autoregressive diffusion transformer alongside visual history through a novel conditioning scheme. Rather than requiring an explicit scene geometry map or visibility tests, the conditioning indicates where characters may appear, allowing the diffusion model to learn their appearance and occlusion. This design enables NPCs to evolve independently of visual generation while maintaining consistent observations across visibility changes, interactions, and respawns. Evaluations in a custom Godot-based first-person shooter game demonstrate improvements in visual fidelity, NPC consistency, and long-horizon stability over existing approaches.

AI.brief_summary: SWAM 在交互式 3D 环境中把 NPC 状态演化与自回归视觉生成解耦：轻量状态模型仅凭动作、结合运动先验与场景修正预测角色状态，再以条件方式引导扩散 transformer 结合视觉历史生成画面。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「内部状态不依赖生成帧即可演化、并在视野外维持实体一致性」的思路，可能与 LVR 中 latent 状态维持与视觉证据筛选相关，可供核查；但该工作是世界模型生成而非多模态推理，迁移价值需判断。
